title: Descent of the orientation equation from compatible affine charts
statement: Fix a finite purity datum P [def-pur-conventions] and composable separated finite-type smooth morphisms f:X->Y,g:Y->Z of pure relative ranks d,e over finite-type k-schemes. Use the actual sigma, diagonal orientations vartheta and ordered Tate multiplication mu [def-pur-composition-model-orientation-coordinates]. Assume the beta-delta-kappa equation on every affine finite-type smooth pair of ranks d,e, for every finite Tate transport. Assume that the shift-removed total Tate power on X is concentrated in degree zero, its H^0 is a rank-one locally free coefficient sheaf, and restriction of automorphisms of that power is injective on every Zariski covering. Then sigma followed by vartheta_(gf) equals the tensor of vartheta_f and Lf*vartheta_g followed by mu. The assertion includes empty X.

proof.text:
In the equality of Step 6 substitute $\vartheta_h=\beta_h\delta_h\alpha_h^{-1}$ and $\alpha_{gf}\kappa=\sigma(\alpha_f\otimes Lf^*\alpha_g)$ from the chart statement. This yields
$$\vartheta_{gf}\sigma(\alpha_f\otimes Lf^*\alpha_g)=\mu(\vartheta_f\otimes Lf^*\vartheta_g)(\alpha_f\otimes Lf^*\alpha_g).$$
The rightmost tensor of $\alpha$ maps is an isomorphism, so cancel it. This proves $(**)$ on every covering chart. Compatibility of the given maps with further open restriction means these are restrictions of the two global arrows in $(**)$, with a common global source and target.

source.place: Step 1: affine model and compatibility of the diagonal orientations

proof.text: Let $A=\vartheta_{gf}\sigma$ and $B=\mu(\vartheta_f\otimes Lf^*\vartheta_g)$, two isomorphisms from $\omega_f\otimes^LLf^*\omega_g$ to $T_X$. They are isomorphisms by the specified orientations, Step 1 and the tensor-mate lemma. Step 7 gives $A|_U=B|_U$, so $(AB^{-1})|_U=1$ on every chart. Apply the automorphism injectivity of Step 8 to obtain $AB^{-1}=1$ and hence $A=B$ globally. If $X$ is empty use the empty cover in the same degree-zero gluing theorem: its equalizer has one element, so every endomorphism of $L[0]$ equals its identity, and shift removal gives the asserted equality for $T_X$ as well. No nonemptiness or connectedness assumption is used.
